articles.title: Luke Littler suffers shock defeat to Krzysztof Ratajski at European Championship Darts in Dortmund
articles.summary: Luke Littler was bidding to win the one major he has yet to take in his career, but was unable to recover after losing seven of the first eight legs of Sunday's quarter-final; Watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
The world No 1 was beaten 10-6 in the quarter-finals on Sunday afternoon as his bid to sweep all of the PDC's major titles before his 20th birthday fell short.

Poland's Ratajski remarkably won seven legs in a row to take a 7-1 lead over the world champion before Littler rallied to pull the game back to 8-6.

But he missed bullseye to hold throw in the 15th leg and Ratajski pinned D16 to move 9-6 ahead.

Littler then failed to take out 121 in the next leg and Ratajski hit D10 to beat The Nuke for the first time in eight meetings.

Reflecting on his victory, Ratajski said: "He started to play very well after the second break. It was 8-2 for me and I had to wait, play my game and focus on my throw.

"He won three or four legs in a row and then I took a chance when he missed a double seven. It was my chance and I took it.

"It's my biggest achievement in the European Championship."

Littler produced the second-best average in the tournament's history against Nathan Aspinall on Saturday evening, but averaged less than 100 on Sunday and hit only six of 16 attempts at double.

It's the latest setback for Littler, who suffered early exits at the World Series of Darts Finals and the World Grand Prix in recent weeks.

Littler will appear on a Netflix special next Friday night when 20 amateur players will attempt to beat him over one leg to win £501,000 before he turns his attention to defending his Grand Slam of Darts title live on Sky Sports in November.

Ratajski to face German favourite in last four

Ratajski will face a home favourite in the semi-finals after Martin Schindler produced an astonishing display to thrash Jonny Clayton 10-1.

In front of a raucous home support, the underdog reeled off nine legs in a row, including a 127 on the bull in the fifth leg and a 167 on the bull in the sixth.

Schindler didn't miss a double in the first seven legs of the match and averaged more than 103 as he pulled off one of the biggest wins of his career.

On the other side of the draw, Gerwyn Price crushed Stephen Bunting 10-3 to book his place in Sunday evening's semi-finals.

Price went eight darts into a nine-darter in the fourth leg of the match, only to miss D12 for the perfect leg. However, he romped into a 7-1 lead and rarely looked in trouble.

Bunting briefly rallied to recover to 7-3, but Price reeled off three more legs for a comprehensive win with a 103 average.

Price will face top seed Ross Smith , who remains in the hunt for a second European Championship title after an impressive 10-6 victory over Luke Woodhouse in the opening match of the day.

He averaged 107 and hit seven 180s before sealing victory in style with a bullseye finish.

articles.title: Sixers' Jaylen Brown responds to former Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown responds to former Boston Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- So, one now has to wonder what qualifies as beef and what falls under the lamb chops category?

The situation surrounding Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown and Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum took another turn recently as Brown left a blue hat emoji--internet slang "cap", which means somebody's lying--on a video of Tatum recounting his feelings of the trade . That then set off alarms in both Boston and Philadelphia as one wonders what's next for the duo as everybody moves forward.

Tatum then had a lengthy response, which can be seen fully transcribed here , as he claims there is now beef between himself and Brown. Tatum expressed frustration that due to Brown no longer being on the Celtics, they can no longer have conversations and such.

After a win over the Milwaukee Bucks , Brown gave a very interesting response.

"I didn't see the full thing, but I saw that he said there's no beef and I think he's right," Brown said. "There's no beef. Jayson comes from a wonderful family. We've accomplished some great things. He's a hell of a basketball player. He got a great PR team. There's no beef, but it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy. You know what I mean? He should stay ready at all times."

Hmm, a great PR team. Lamb chops. Gravy. What exactly is Brown trying to say?

"Just, that's what it is," Brown said. "No beef. It should never, ever be that. It's just basketball. We're both blessed. It might be a little lamb chop. We'll be all right."

Tatum added he wants to have a conversation with Brown.

"We both got so much stuff in front of us," the 2024 finals MVP said of any convos. "So, at the end of the day, we both … He's got to do what he's got to do for his team. I got to do what I do for my team. Jayson's a great guy. Like I said, great family, hell of a basketball player, hell of a PR team. There's no beef, but it be a little lamb chop."

So, lamb chops. Not fully beef. Brown is a member of the Sixers. Tatum is leading the Celtics. Obviously, there's something going on between the two of them, but it remains to be seen how everybody will handle this as time moves on.

"Look, like I said, there's no beef," Brown finished. "The PR and all that type stuff, it is what it is, but I think we just both focused on what's in front of us."

The Sixers and the Celtics will match up for the first time on Nov. 10 at the Xfinity Mobile Arena.

articles.title: Wembanyama scores 23 as Spurs beat Mavericks for first win of NBA season
articles.summary: Joel Embiid posts triple-double as 76ers handle Bucks. Devin Booker posts 43 to help Suns down Warriors.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has scored 23 points as the visiting San Antonio Spurs have earned their first win of the season by defeating the short-handed Dallas Mavericks 122-106 in the second of back-to-back games for both teams.

Dylan Harper added 22 points on Saturday, De’Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle scored 19 each, Julian Champagnie scored 12 off the bench and Devin Vassell tallied 11 points for San Antonio. Wembanyama also posted seven rebounds and four blocks.

Rookie Sergio De Larrea’s 21 points led Dallas. Marcus Sasser, PJ Washington and Daniel Gafford scored 12 apiece, Zaccharie Risacher had 11 and Naji Marshall contributed 10.

San Antonio led 68-60 at the break behind Fox’s 15 points, 12 from Wembanyama and 11 by Castle. De Larrea paced the Mavericks with 13 points off the bench with Washington and Marshall adding 10 each.

The Spurs expanded their lead to 14 early in the third before Dallas roared back, scoring 22 of the ensuing 29 points and regaining the lead at 85-84. The game went to the fourth quarter with San Antonio up 92-89 as Castle and Wembanyama hit late threes.

Embiid posts triple-double as 76ers handle Bucks

Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double, and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead the Philadelphia 76ers to a 127-116 home win over the Milwaukee Bucks.

Embiid finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for Philadelphia.

Tyrese Maxey pitched in with 26 points for the Sixers while VJ Edgecombe made five three-pointers as part of a 17-point, 13-rebound performance.

While the Sixers are 3-0 on the young season, the Bucks fell to 0-3 despite eight players scoring in double figures. Jaime Jaquez Jr led Milwaukee with 21 points while Kel’el Ware had 19 points and 13 rebounds off the bench for the visitors.

The teams were tied at 82-82 with four minutes left in the third quarter before the Sixers ended the period on a 15-5 push. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Maxey each made a three-pointer during that surge.

Philadelphia started to pull away early in the fourth.

Embiid’s jumper gave the hosts a 113-98 lead with six minutes left. The Sixers still held a comfortable advantage at 117-108 with 3:18 to go before the Bucks rattled off six in a row in just over a minute to make it a three-point game.

Philadelphia knocked down five three-pointers in the first quarter – three by Edgecombe – en route to a 34-25 lead after 12 minutes.

Booker, Suns continue Warriors’ rough start to season

Devin Booker had 43 points, seven assists and seven rebounds, and the host Phoenix Suns beat Golden State 131-122 to send the Warriors to their worst start of a season in almost two decades.

Miles Bridges scored 16 points, and Dillon Brooks added 15 points for the Suns, setting a franchise record for points in a home opener.

Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 26 points and nine rebounds, and De’Anthony Melton scored 20 of his 25 points in the second half for the skeleton-crew Warriors.

Golden State was without starters Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski and Draymond Green and reserve Al Horford.

Brandon Williams added 20 points while Lendeborg made six of the Warriors’ 17 three-pointers and Melton had four.

Melton scored 13 points in the third quarter when the Warriors used a 12-0 run to take a 73-71 lead before the Suns came back. Booker’s four-point play with 35 seconds left in the third quarter made it 99-89 for Phoenix.

Luke Kennard’s three-pointer pushed the Suns’ lead to 117-102 with 6:07 remaining in the game.

Kennard had 11 points and three three-pointers in his Suns debut after missing the season opener with a knee injury.

The Warriors made 17 of 39 three-pointers and turned 19 offensive rebounds into 26 points.

Lendeborg had six points on a pair of threes, and Graham Ike had six points and five rebounds in the first quarter when the Warriors took an early seven-point lead and had a 25-22 edge at the end of the quarter.

articles.title: PV Sindhu loses French Open final to world No. 1 An Se Young after spirited fight
articles.summary: PV Sindhu came agonisingly close to ending her long wait for a victory over world No.
articles.body: PV Sindhu came agonisingly close to ending her long wait for a victory over world No. 1 An Se Young but eventually fell short in the final of the French Open Super 750 badminton tournament on Sunday. The Indian shuttler claimed the opening game against the Olympic champion but could not sustain the momentum, going down 21-16, 11-21, 12-21 after a spirited battle in Paris.The defeat extended Sindhu's winless run against the South Korean to 11 matches, but the two-time Olympic medallist had plenty of positives to take from the contest. An, meanwhile, secured her fourth French Open title and her 11th title of the season, further underlining her dominance on the international circuit."I fought for every point. I could win the first game, and I was happy about it. But in the second game, it was equal until five-all or 5-4. After that, she took a lead and maintained it," Sindhu said after the match."Even in the third game, I should have maintained the lead from 8-5. Unfortunately, she converted that into 11-9. That's where I felt the difference was. But there are a lot of positives to take from this match. Going forward, I need to work on them," she added.Sindhu makes strong start to take opening gameSindhu used her reach and attacking strokes to good effect in the opening game, which lasted 20 minutes. It was only the second time in her career that she had managed to win a game against An, having failed to beat the Korean in their previous 10 meetings.The opening exchanges were closely contested, with the two engaging in lengthy rallies and net battles to move from 4-4 to 7-7. During one such exchange, An rushed forward to play a shot but ended up hitting Sindhu on the face with the shuttle.Sindhu edged ahead at the interval with an overhead cross-court smash and soon extended her advantage to 15-11, capitalising on An's judgement errors near the backline.The Korean attempted to fight back as Sindhu made a few unforced errors, but the Indian maintained control. A disguised slice helped her earn six game points, and although An saved two with a deceptive drop and an angled cross-court return, another shot from the South Korean sailed long to hand Sindhu the opening game.An Se Young responds to level the matchThe world No. 1 came out aggressively after the change of ends, racing to a 3-0 lead. Sindhu attempted to close the gap with a cross-court smash and a body smash, but An's sharp net play kept her ahead.A brilliant net shot and a 30-shot rally helped the Korean maintain her advantage before two powerful smashes gave her a four-point lead at the interval. An continued to dictate the rallies after the break, moving to 13-7 as Sindhu struggled to maintain consistency. The Indian's errors mounted, allowing the South Korean to claim nine of the next 10 points and move to 17-8.An eventually earned 12 game points. Sindhu saved three before the Olympic champion converted the fourth opportunity to level the match and force a decider.Sindhu's early lead slips away in the deciderThe deciding game produced another intense contest, with Sindhu battling both An's quality and the sideways drift on court. A 36-shot rally ended with the Indian hitting wide, but she responded strongly to establish a 8-5 lead.An fought back with a smash to level the score at 8-8 before moving ahead after pouncing on a loose shot at the net. A body smash and another attack towards Sindhu's backhand gave the Korean a two-point advantage at the interval.Having won six of the last seven points in the first half of the decider, An carried that momentum forward to move to 13-9. Her shot-making grew sharper as she stretched the lead to 18-10, leaving Sindhu with little room to recover.A shot from Sindhu sailing long handed An eight match points, and the South Korean sealed the title at the first opportunity to complete another victory over the Indian.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Roberto Viciedo y Eva Rebol reinan en el cierre por equipos del Hyatlón Ambar Tour
articles.standfirst: La pareja ha ganado el Dobles Mixtos Élite en la segunda cita, disputada en La Nucía
articles.summary: La pareja ha ganado el Dobles Mixtos Élite en la segunda cita, disputada en La Nucía
articles.body: El Combat Sports Center de La Nucía ha sido escenario de un cierre épico para la segunda parada del Hyatlón Ambar Tour. Tras la intensidad de las pruebas individuales del sábado, este domingo el protagonismo ha recaído en el trabajo en equipo con la disputa de las modalidades de dobles y relevos en categorías mixtas, femeninas y masculinas. El gran nombre de la jornada ha sido el de Roberto Viciedo, quien junto a Eva Rebol se ha alzado con la primera posición en la categoría de Dobles Mixtos Élite. Viciedo confirma así su extraordinario estado de forma, encadenando este triunfo con su reciente y sonada victoria de la semana pasada en el Hyrox de Valencia (donde ganó tanto en Dobles Élite Masculino como en Single Élite Masculino). En el resto de las categorías, la gloria fue para Víctor Esparza y José Antonio Henarejos, campeones en Dobles Masculino Élite, y para la dupla formada por Laura Ortiz y Emma Llopis, intratables en el Dobles Femenino Élite. Los equipos tuvieron que hacer frente al temido formato H6, una exigencia continua de resistencia y fuerza sin pausas entre segmentos. El reto obligó a los atletas a intercalar de manera ininterrumpida tramos de un kilómetro de carrera a pie con las seis estaciones funcionales del circuito: 1.000 metros de SkiErg, 50 metros de Sled Push, 80 metros de Burpee Broad Jump, 1.000 metros de RowErg, 100 metros de Sandbag Lunges y, para el colofón final, 100 repeticiones de Wall Balls. Matrix Fitness, patrocinador oficial del Hyatlón, se encargó de proporcionar la maquinaria, las pesas y adecuar el espacio de competición con un equipamiento de primer nivel mundial. El evento brilló tanto en la pista como fuera de ella gracias al despliegue de las marcas patrocinadoras. Los asistentes y participantes pudieron recuperar fuerzas con la innovadora Ambar Triple Cero Probiótica de Cervezas Ambar y la energía garantizada por los productos de 226ers en la zona de avituallamiento. Joma aportó el estilo con su stand de zapatillas y equipamiento oficial de atletismo y Hyatlón, mientras que Noofit deslumbró a los presentes con su avanzada tecnología de monitorización del ejercicio físico. MARCA, como medio oficial, se encargó de dar cobertura y llevar los resúmenes del evento a todos los aficionados. Durante la jornada, la organización hizo entrega de un obsequio a Jessica Gomans, concejala del Ayuntamiento de La Nucía, en profundo agradecimiento por la confianza y las facilidades prestadas para asentar el evento en la ciudad. Esta prueba, impulsada por la Federación Española de Triatlón (FETRI), ha sido posible gracias a la inestimable colaboración del propio Ayuntamiento, la Diputación de Alicante y la Generalitat Valenciana, responsables de la cesión de las instalaciones. Asimismo, la dirección del circuito ha querido extender un agradecimiento muy especial a todos los voluntarios, cuya labor ha sido el motor fundamental para el perfecto desarrollo de la prueba. Con los deberes hechos y el éxito rotundo en territorio alicantino, el circuito nacional no pisa el freno. El Hyatlón Ambar Tour hará las maletas para celebrar su tercera parada en Las Palmas de Gran Canaria los próximos 13, 14 y 15 de noviembre, antes de poner el broche de oro definitivo al tour en la gran final de Zaragoza, programada para los días 28 y 29 de noviembre.

articles.title: LSU's Lane Kiffin explains thinking behind aggressive fourth down decision
articles.summary: LSU football head coach Lane Kiffin explained the decision making process behind his aggressive fourth down choice in the second quarter.
articles.body:
LSU football took an early chance with a seven-point lead at Auburn. On its first drive of the second quarter, head coach Lane Kiffin faced a decision on whether to keep the offense on the field on fourth and two. He went with the offense, and the Tigers converted.

"Book was fourth and one to go, fourth and two punt," Kiffin said. "I just really felt good about our matchups in this game, how our offense was playing coming into the game."

On the initial fourth down, a direct snap went to Dilin Jones. He tossed it back to Sam Leavitt, who threw it to Trey'Dez Green for the easy first down. Nine plays later, Leavitt connected with Green again for a 15-yard touchdown. It extended the lead to 17-3.

LSU was three for four on fourth-down attempts in the 38-17 victory. Leavitt moved the chains with a quarterback keeper on fourth and one in the purple and gold's opening drive of the second half. The third conversion came in the fourth quarter when Leavitt found Winston Watkins for a 14-yard pass.

"There were going to be some situations where I told myself we're going be playing around the side of being aggressive and putting it on our players because it just felt like it was a really good matchup game for us. Just through the week and watching tape and how we matchup with them, our [defensive] line against their [offensive] line and our receivers on certain reads."

LSU beat Auburn 38-17 on Saturday, giving the Tigers their first SEC road win in over two years.

articles.title: How long is Jalen Duren out? Hamstring injury updates, return timeline for Pistons star
articles.summary: Detroit will be without the center for a few weeks.
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons are off to a fast start to the season, winning their first two games, but they will have to move forward without one of their best players.

Center Jalen Duren is set to miss the next few weeks after he suffered a right hamstring strain against the Miami Heat on Friday night. Duren had a strange offseason, as he waited to sign a big contract extension with the team, even missing the first few practices in training camp while he waited to agree on the big deal.

Last year, Duren had a career-best season in which he played 70 games, and it helped him earn his big extension in the offseason. Duren was Detroit's leading rebounder and second-leading scorer last year, proving to be an important complement next to Cade Cunningham.

Now, Detroit will have to find a way to win games without Duren. Here's the latest on Duren's injury status.

The Pistons announced that Duren will be sidelined for at least two weeks with a right hamstring injury, but Duren will likely be out for longer than that. The Pistons medical staff will re-evaluate the center's hamstring in two weeks, at which point they will decide on next steps.

Duren suffered the injury in the Pistons' win on Friday night, and he was already ruled out for Sunday's game before the team announced the full diagnosis. As the season just began, the Pistons will not rush Duren back and instead make sure he is fully healthy the next time he returns to action.

Typically, this kind of injury in the NBA costs the player between 2-3 weeks of action, which is around eight regular season games.

With Duren out, the Pistons will rely on new forward John Collins and backup center Paul Reed to help replace the center's production. The Pistons' schedule does not get any easier, as they travel to play the Philadelphia 76ers and New York Knicks in their next two games.

articles.title: Brent Venables reacts to Oklahoma's win over Mississippi State
articles.summary: Brent Venables praises Oklahoma's ability to win but says costly mistakes made the Mississippi State game closer than necessary.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners bounced-back after collapsing against the Kentucky Wildcats in the fourth quarter a week ago. The Sooners defeated the Mississippi State Bulldogs , 23-15 on the road.

Oklahoma dominated the game from start to finish, outgaining the Bulldogs 467 to 352. Quarterback John Mateer was excellent, completing 22-of-29 passes for 283 yards and two scores, while rushing for 37 yards on nine carries. Oklahoma had a season-high 184 yards on the ground on 4.5 yards per carry.

Head coach Brent Venables reacted to the performance after the game.

"I'm proud of our guys, our team, coaches, and players for figuring out how to win a game the same way, somehow," Venables said. "Made it hard at times. It didn't have to be as hard. But if you make some of the mistakes we made, you are going to be sitting there right there at the end hoping to close them out."

The win offered encouraging signs for an Oklahoma offense that had struggled to find consistency through the first half of the season. Mateer's efficiency through the air, combined with the Sooners' best rushing performance of the year, gave the offense a more balanced attack and helped Oklahoma control the game statistically. That progress will be important to build on as the Sooners look to establish a more reliable identity on offense.

Still, Venables' comments underscored that there is work left to do. Oklahoma's ability to move the ball was a positive, but missed opportunities and costly mistakes kept the Bulldogs within reach late in the game. The Sooners will look to clean up those issues heading into their next matchup, carrying the confidence of a road win while knowing that finishing stronger will be essential against tougher competition.

articles.title: Predicting Cowboys final 11 games of 2026; what will final record be?
articles.summary: The Cowboys have stumbled out the gate. How does that change our game-by-game prediction for the rest of the schedule?
articles.body:
Things haven't exactly gone according to plan for the Dallas Cowboys this season. Once again, local media and fans have eaten the cheese, to borrow a Bill Parcells phrase. All offseason, a turnaround from back-to-back seven win seasons was preached, as there was excitement for the process used to find a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker.

Instead of that joy, it turns out the concerns over the 2025 hiring of head coach Brian Schottenheimer appear to be well founded, and the "same old" thought process for Jerry Jones teams seems to be as accurate as ever. What does that leave for the rest of the season, with 11 games remaining?

In May, when the schedule was announced, we predicted a 4-2 start for the club; that's turned into a 2-4 record and a ton of questions. The rest of the schedule? Here's a look at what was predicted then, and what is predicted now, starting with Monday night's game in Philadelphia.

Week 7: at Philadelphia Eagles , 7:30 p.m., Monday, Oct. 26, ESPN

Original Prediction: The Cowboys don't fear the Eagles whatsover, in Philly or at home. They'll come out hot and fans will be able to see how well Christian Parker knows his former team. Pick: Cowboys 31, Eagles 21.

Updated Prediction: In the war of attrition, the Cowboys are facing their inability to win under the lights. Schottenheimer teams are 1-7-1 in primetime. The Eagles are decimated though. A loss here might end the BS era mid-season. Pick: Cowboys 31, Eagles 21. (3-4)

Week 8: vs. Arizona Cardinals , Noon, Nov. 1, FOX

Original Prediction: The Cowboys finally get to face the Cardinals without Kyler Murray. Whoops, that was the case last year when Jacoby Brissett just played like the Dallas Dominator. This is revenge. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 17 .

Updated Prediction: The Cardinals are giving up 37 ppg outside of Los Angeles' SoFi Stadium. Again, a loss here is a fireable offense. Pick: Cowboys 27, Cardinals 17 . (4-4)

Week 9: at Indianapolis Colts , Noon, Nov. 8, CBS

Original Prediction: The Cowboys will travel to face their former punching bag at quarterback Daniel Jons. He hears voices in his head, but this isn't Randy Orton. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 24 .

Updated Prediction: It's more likely than not the Colts arrive at this game with a 2-6 record, but at least they'll be at home. The Cowboys should enjoy the early kickoff again, making their way above .500 and temporarily giving hope to the fanbase. Pick: Cowboys 24, Colts 21 . (5-4)

Week 10: vs. San Francisco 49ers, 3:25 p.m., Nov. 15, FOX

Original Prediction: Kyle Shanahan and company make their way to Dallas with a renewed offensive attack. Pick: 49ers 28, Cowboys 24 .

Updated Prediction: Flip side, the 49ers should enter this contest at 8-0, semi-fresh of a Week 8 bye week. Cowboys fans are already selling their tickets; it's going to be a red wave in AT&T Stadium. Pick 49ers 36, Cowboys 24. (5-5)

Week 11: vs. Tennessee Titans, Noon, Nov. 22, CBS

Original Prediction: The Titans are working to return from the grave with a renewed offense that will bring old friend Tony Pollard back to town. He's used to being disappointed in this city. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 10 .

Updated Prediction: Tennessee might be the worst team in the league, Dallas should still be able to dominate this club and get back above .500. Pick: Cowboys 27, Titans 10 . (6-5).

Week 12: vs. Philadelphia Eagles, 3:30 p.m., Thursday Nov. 26, FOX

Original Prediction: The Cowboys have won four straight Thanksgiving Day games. It's going to be an ugly game, but they sweep the Eagles for 2026. Pick: Cowboys 26, Eagles 24 .

Updated Prediction: The Eagles should be relatively healthier and in a groove for this rematch, which doesn't bode well for the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. This will be the Joe Milton experience; ugh. Pick Eagles 27, Cowboys 24. (6-6)

Week 13: at Seattle Seahawks, 7:15 p.m., Monday, Nov. 7, ESPN

Original Prediction: There are so many ties between these two teams who are rivals that hate each other despite not playing every season. The Super Bowl champs, hosting Dallas at a night game? Bring the ear plugs. Pick: Seahawks 31, Cowboys 27 .

Updated Prediction: Sam Darnold isn't having the same campaign he did in 2025, but the primetime issues for the Cowboys return. Just too much time in the day to get in their own heads, plus the Seattle crowd is super loud and hates their guts. Pick: Seahawks 31, Cowboys 27 . (6-7)

Week 15: vs. Los Angeles Rams 3:25 p.m., Dec. 20, FOX

Original Prediction: The Cowboys have low-key dominated Sean McVay's Rams since they lost to them in the playoffs following the 2018 season. Pick: Cowboys 44, Rams 24 .

Updated Prediction: A fresh Myles Garrett after missing the first half of the season is not something anyone could've predicted. The Rams are hitting their stride in the second half. Pick: Rams 34, Cowboys 24 . (6-8)

Week 16: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars , 7:20 p.m., Dec. 27, NBC

Original Prediction: The Jaguars are actually good? What do we do with this type of information? Pick: Jaguars 27, Cowboys 24 .

Updated Prediction: The Jaguars might be the AFC's best team, but predicting a home upset in this one. Pick: Cowboys 27, Jaguars 24 . (7-8)

Week 17: vs. New York Giants, Noon, Jan. 3, 2027, FOX

Original Prediction: The Giants are still the Giants. Pick: Cowboys 38, Giants 10 .

Updated Prediction: No change. Pick: Cowboys 38, Giants 10 . (8-8)

Week 18: at Washington Commanders, TBD, Jan. 9/10, TBD

Original Prediction: The Cowboys have closed out the season vs Washington more often than not in recent years. Health will determine the season, so health will determine this game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Commanders 3 .

Updated Prediction: No change. Pick: Cowboys 31, Commanders 3 .(9-8)

Original Prediction: We've got the Cowboys finishing the 2026 NFL season at 12-5.

Updated Prediction: 9-8, NFC East winners because the division is horrible.

articles.title: Buccaneers have played in 12 straight one-score games
articles.summary: If the league office has a favorite team, it's currently the Buccaneers.
articles.body:
If the league office has a favorite team, it's currently the Buccaneers. Every week, their games remain exciting because they're undecided down to the end.

Tampa Bay has a current streak of 12 straight one-score games. Via NBC Sports research, it's tied for the third-longest streak of one-score games since the merger.

The 1989-90 Chargers had a 14-game streak, and the 2014-15 Ravens had a 13-game streak.

The bad news for the Bucs is that they're 3-9 in those games — and 1-5 on the season. They'll get quarterback Baker Mayfield back today in Carolina; he missed three games with a dislocated thumb suffered in Week 3 against the Vikings.

The good news for the Bucs is that, since 2020, they're 10-2 against the Panthers.

Ole Book on Saturday night's 1-0 home win against Eintracht Frankfurt : "It was definitely well-deserved! Sure, it felt a bit like a hard-fought victory. But we built up more and more pressure in the second half and didn't allow anything at the back, so it was definitely a well-deserved win!"

... the next Bundesliga match without conceding a goal: "We can definitely see that we have very, very good stability. That's something that set the team apart last season as well. We're working on areas where we want to play even better soccer. I also think you can already see a difference. We're already a bit more dominant than we were at times last season. But you have to expect that things won't all click into place overnight, especially since we're also dealing with some absences in the creative department."

… on the past week's successes in Baku and against Frankfurt: "Of course, we feel much better now that we've secured two very important wins. In the Champions League, it was crucial to keep our chances of reaching the Round of 16 alive. And in the league, it's also a great feeling to be at the top—at least for one night."

… on the upcoming week with matches against Werder Bremen and Bayern Munich: "These are very important games for us, absolutely. But we said the same thing before the last few games, too—it's one game after another. We're currently playing every three days, which is an enormous strain. That's why it's all the more impressive that we were able to step up our game as the match progressed yesterday. We know we don't really have a break. The players know what's coming our way next week."

articles.title: Watch: Arsenal loanee makes top diving save
articles.summary: Tommy Setford made a fantastic save for Stevenage against MK Dons on Saturday, but the Arsenal loanee couldn’t stop his team slipping to a 1-0 defeat.Photo v...
articles.body:
Tommy Setford made a fantastic save for Stevenage against MK Dons on Saturday, but the Arsenal loanee couldn't stop his team slipping to a 1-0 defeat.

Arsenal loanee Tommy Setford has made a strong start to his loan spell with Stevenage , making the lineup for all seven of their League One fixtures since his debut, and keeping a clean sheet in two of his four games since the October international break.

Setford was away with the England u21s over the break, and Stevenage had to play an EFL Trophy fixture without him. But he's slotted straight back into the lineup, and produced some of his best performances of the season so far.

First there was the clean sheet in a 1-0 win over Wigan Athletic , then another in a 3-0 victory over Plymouth Argyle . But perhaps Setford's best save was against MK Dons over the weekend, despite his team ultimately losing the match.

With the scores still level in the second half, MK Dons striker Sam Nombe won the ball high up the pitch, finding himself with a two-on-one against the last defender.

Nombe threaded a pass through to Aaron Collins , beating the defence and leaving Setford as Stevenage's only hope. The goalkeeper charged out to close down the shot, and he made a fantastic diving save to deny his opponent.

The highlights are available below, with the save at the timestamp 1:12.

As mentioned, the away side went on to win the match anyway. Nombe got on the end of a cross in the 81st minute after another cheap concession of possession by Stevenage, and a scrambling Setford couldn't get across his line quickly enough that time.

But Setford is playing regularly, keeping clean sheets every other game, and making some great saves. This is largely what he would have hoped for from his loan spell, and long may it continue.

articles.title: Baylor makes head coach decision after 2 straight losses
articles.summary: Baylor Bears make a major head coach decision after two straight losses, and the move could reshape the Big 12 race.
articles.body:
The Baylor Bears lost 25-24 at Kansas on Saturday after a Baylor field goal was blocked near the end of regulation. The result snapped the Bears' 14-game winning streak against the Jayhawks and dropped them to 4-3. The Bears entered the game 4-2.

Seventh-year head coach Dave Aranda guided Baylor to a 12-2 record, the Big 12 title and a Sugar Bowl win over Ole Miss in 2021, the best season in program history. But Saturday's loss was the Bears' second straight, and pressure had been building since a 5-7 finish in 2025. By Sunday morning, Baylor's administration had reached a decision.

Baylor fires Dave Aranda, names Joe Klanderman interim head coach

Baylor has fired Aranda, sources told ESPN's Pete Thamel. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman will serve as interim head coach for the rest of the regular season.

Aranda finishes 40-40 in seven seasons, including 26-32 in Big 12 play, with four losing seasons in his first six years.

He arrived from LSU, where he was associate head coach and defensive coordinator, and went 2-7 in the COVID-shortened 2020 season.

Who is Joe Klanderman, Baylor's interim head coach?

Klanderman joined Baylor this year after seven seasons at Kansas State, the last six as defensive coordinator. Thamel reported the hire on Dec. 11, 2025.

He previously helped North Dakota State win four FCS national championships as defensive backs coach from 2014 to 2018. Through Week 8, Baylor's defense ranks second in the Big 12 in total yards allowed (301.6 per game) and third in points allowed (16.1) with Klanderman calling plays.

His first game as interim coach comes Friday against UCF, giving Baylor a short week to adjust after the change.

articles.title: WATCH: Devaughn Vele catches fourth-quarter TD pass from Tyler Shough
articles.summary: Tyler Shough and Devaughn Vele went for it on fourth down, scoring a clutch New Orleans Saints TD pass on fourth down against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
There you go. The New Orleans Saints chose to go for broke on fourth down against the Pittsburgh Steelers, having gotten stopped on three straight running plays at the goal line. This time they asked Tyler Shough to throw to his wide receiver Devaughn Vele in the flat, and the big receiver came through. He caught the scoring pass for a game-tying touchdown pass.

Vele has been a consistent threat for the Saints on third downs, but this was just his third touchdown of the season. He's a valuable target on critical downs at 6-foot-5, 210 pounds, and New Orleans is beginning to use his skills more and more. It's exactly what you hope to see out of an offense that's struggled to keep pressure on their opponents. When you're in the red zone, throwing to a receiver who is taller and stronger than his opponents should be an easy call. With Jordyn Tyson hopeful to return after the bye week, it's important that Vele continue to see targets in the top-three receivers along with Chris Olave and the team's first-round pick.

articles.title: Arizona football opens as small underdog at Texas Tech
articles.summary: The Arizona Wildcats have taken care of business against the Big 12’s mid to lesser competition. Now comes an opportunity for Arizona to prove it belongs in...
articles.body:
The Arizona Wildcats have taken care of business against the Big 12's mid to lesser competition. Now comes an opportunity for Arizona to prove it belongs in the conversation for the conference's top teams.

Arizona (6-1) travels to Lubbock Saturday for a 9:00 a.m. MST tilt against Texas Tech in a game the Red Raiders are favored to win by 4.5 points. The over/under is 55.5 points.

Arizona is coming off a 39-3 bludgeoning of Iowa State, which moved the Wildcats' record against the spread (ATS) to 3-4 on the year. Arizona has covered in three consecutive games, winning by an average of 28 points.

The Wildcats are heading on the road for the fourth time this fall, having previously lost at BYU and won at Washington and West Virginia.

Arizona is 5-27 all-time against Texas Tech. Last year the Red Raiders beat the Wildcats 28-22 in Tucson, and before that the last matchup was in 2019, a 28-14 home win for Arizona.

Arizona's last trip to Lubbock came in 1989, a 24-14 loss. Historically, the UA has a 1-13-1 record in Lubbock with the lone win coming in 1935.

Texas Tech (6-1) is coming off a 37-24 loss at Cincinnati in a game the Red Raiders were favored to win by 11.5 points. The loss will move Texas Tech out of the top 10 in the rankings, and another defeat could all but end the Red Raiders' playoff hopes.

After a noisy offseason, Texas Tech has looked underwhelming for much of the fall. The Red Raiders barely slipped by Houston in their Big 12 opener and trailed Colorado into the third quarter.

Texas Tech was outclassed by Cincinnati despite holding the Bearcats to 172 passing yards. The Red Raiders committed three turnovers, one an interception by quarterback Will Hammond and the other two fumbles (one by Hammond).

Hammond has thrown as many interceptions as touchdowns (6) this season.

The Red Raiders nevertheless face a big advantage playing at home Saturday. Texas Tech is riding a 12-game winning streak at Galaxy Stadium. The program's last home loss came to Colorado in November 2024.

articles.title: Red Wings Executive Spotted Scouting Original 8 Team Amid Larkin Trade Speculation
articles.summary: Red Wings assistant GM Kris Draper scouts the Canadiens again as Dylan Larkin trade speculation continues. Here's what the latest visit means.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings continue to do their homework on the Montreal Canadiens , and the latest development involving assistant general manager Kris Draper is raising even more questions about Dylan Larkin's future . Draper was reportedly spotted scouting Montreal for the second time in four days, adding another intriguing wrinkle to the ongoing trade speculation surrounding Detroit's former captain.

With Montreal still absent from Larkin's list of approved trade destinations, there is one major obstacle preventing the Canadiens from becoming a legitimate option. However, Detroit's continued scouting activity suggests the organization wants to be prepared if that situation changes.

Kris Draper Spotted at Another Canadiens Game

Draper attended Friday night's matchup between the Canadiens and Chicago Blackhawks at the United Center, according to October 24 reporting on the Red Wings executive's latest scouting trip . His appearance came just three days after he was identified in the press box for Montreal's October 20 game against the San Jose Sharks at the Bell Centre.

That is an interesting sequence considering everything happening around the Red Wings organization right now. Detroit is evaluating potential returns for Larkin while also navigating the unresolved contract situation involving defenseman Simon Edvinsson.

Draper isn't the only member of Detroit's front office who has been watching Montreal. Red Wings professional scout Chris Yzerman has also attended Canadiens games, giving the organization multiple opportunities to evaluate potential trade assets.

Of course, attending NHL games is part of a front-office executive's job, and there is no confirmation that every visit was specifically related to Larkin. Still, Draper's repeated appearances have become particularly interesting because of what a prominent NHL insider recently revealed.

Pierre LeBrun Confirms Red Wings Are Scouting Montreal

The significance of Detroit's scouting activity became clearer when Pierre LeBrun addressed the Larkin situation on Thursday's edition of Insider Trading . LeBrun reported that the Red Wings are actively evaluating Montreal's roster in case Larkin eventually agrees to consider the Canadiens.

"Detroit is actively scouting the Montreal Canadiens of late, among other teams of course, but doing their due diligence on the Canadiens in person just in case Dylan Larkin does add Montreal to that list," LeBrun explained .

That is the important distinction in this situation, because Detroit's scouting activity is confirmed through reporting rather than simply being another fan-generated trade idea. However, there has been no confirmation that Larkin has changed his mind about Montreal or that an agreement between the two organizations is approaching.

The Canadiens have been mentioned repeatedly as a potential destination because they possess young talent and prospects that could interest Detroit. For interim general manager Shawn Horcoff, understanding the value of those players would be important if Montreal eventually becomes an approved trading partner.

Dylan Larkin Still Has One Major Obstacle to Montreal Trade

The biggest problem is that Larkin currently has no obligation to accept a trade to the Canadiens. His contract includes a full no-movement clause, meaning Detroit cannot send him to Montreal without his approval.

As we previously reported , Larkin expanded his list of acceptable destinations from three teams to 10 earlier this month. All 10 organizations are based in the United States, leaving Montreal on the outside despite considerable speculation about the Canadiens' interest.

That matters because Montreal could theoretically offer Detroit the most attractive return and still be unable to complete a trade. Unless Larkin changes his position, the Red Wings would have to continue exploring other destinations that he has already approved.

There is also the possibility that Larkin's stance eventually changes as the season progresses. Montreal's strong young core and need for another established center could make the Canadiens an interesting option, but any such decision belongs entirely to Larkin.

What Could Montreal Offer the Red Wings?

From Detroit's perspective, the Canadiens represent an intriguing potential trade partner because of their collection of young players and prospects. One name that has previously surfaced in the discussion is Michael Hage , Montreal's 2024 first-round draft pick who is currently playing at the University of Michigan.

As we previously reported , Hage has been identified as a prospect who could interest the Red Wings in a potential Larkin deal. His combination of offensive skill, center experience, and long-term upside makes him the type of player Detroit could evaluate while considering its future down the middle.

The Red Wings have reportedly been exploring the market for young centers, including highly regarded prospects who have not yet established themselves in the NHL. That approach would give Detroit an opportunity to acquire a potential future building block rather than focusing exclusively on established veterans.

However, trading Larkin for prospects would also create an immediate problem for the Red Wings. Detroit would be surrendering its most established center without necessarily acquiring someone capable of replacing his production during the current season.

That is why Horcoff must carefully evaluate any potential offer before moving forward. The organization cannot afford to sacrifice one of its most important players simply because a package contains recognizable prospects or valuable draft picks.

Nick Suzuki Injury Adds Another Interesting Factor

Montreal's situation has also become more complicated following an upper-body injury to captain Nick Suzuki . The Canadiens' top center is expected to miss approximately two to four weeks, creating an immediate challenge for a team attempting to remain competitive in the Eastern Conference.

Larkin would provide Montreal with an established offensive center capable of playing significant minutes in all situations. His arrival could also help strengthen the Canadiens' depth once Suzuki returns, although there is no indication that the injury has changed Larkin's willingness to play in Montreal.

For Detroit, the more important issue remains the potential return rather than Montreal's immediate injury concerns. If the Canadiens eventually become an option, Horcoff would need to determine whether their prospects and established players offer greater value than packages available from teams already on Larkin's approved list.

Red Wings Continue Preparing for Possible Dylan Larkin Trade

Draper's latest scouting appearance does not mean a Dylan Larkin trade is imminent, but it adds another concrete detail to a situation that has generated considerable attention. Detroit's front office appears determined to evaluate its options thoroughly rather than limit its preparation to teams currently on Larkin's approved list.

That preparation could become valuable if Montreal eventually enters the picture. With Larkin carrying an $8.7 million annual salary-cap hit through the 2030-31 season, any potential deal would require careful consideration of both the return package and the acquiring team's financial commitments.

For now, the Red Wings have not publicly announced an agreement involving Larkin, and Montreal remains outside his reported list of acceptable destinations. Nevertheless, Draper's second Canadiens scouting appearance in the same week gives Detroit fans another development worth watching as the organization continues searching for a resolution.

articles.title: SPFL Roundup: Rangers run riot, United win five-goal thriller and Celtic win again
articles.summary: The 10th Scottish Premiership gameweek of the season is in the books, so let’s take a look at all the action across the top flight as Rangers and Celtic both...
articles.body:
The 10th Scottish Premiership gameweek of the season is in the books, so let's take a look at all the action across the top flight as Rangers and Celtic both picked up crucial points in their ongoing battle for top spot.

Rangers ran riot at Ibrox on Saturday afternoon, putting four past a St. Johnstone team who proved little threat to Derek McInnes' side.

Kevin Kelsy opened the scoring on the half-hour mark when he rounded off a fast 'Gers break by poking the ball home from close range. Ryan Don Naderi doubled his side's lead in the 61st minute, before Kelsy netted again just five minutes later to put Rangers comfortably ahead.

Things went from bad to worse for the Saints when Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card for a foul on Nico Raskin inside Rangers' half. The fourth goal came from Tochi Chukuani in the final moments of the match; the Danish midfielder found the bottom corner from inside the area.

A five-goal thriller took place at Tannadice, with the Tangerines ultimately coming out on top in a topsy-turvy affair with Aberdeen.

Zidane Iqbal gave United an early lead with a stunning strike, but they were quickly pegged back by Nesta Guiness-Walker, who fired into the side netting from 10 yards. However, the hosts regained their lead almost immediately through Dylan Tait, who ran the match, to be honest, when he found the net from a corner.

Aberdeen came out firing in the second half and got themselves level again early on, this time thanks to Connor Ronan, who picked out the bottom corner from distance with a lovely finish. However, the eventual winner did go the way of Jim Goodwin's side, when Zachary Sapsford headed home Tait's cross to secure all three points.

It was an incredibly one-sided match at The Falkirk Stadium, which saw the hosts claim a convincing 3-0 win over Kilmarnock.

Killie goalkeeper Calum Ferrie stopped it from being more, making a whopping seven saves despite the best efforts of the defenders in front of him, who netted two own goals between them, those being Cathal McCarthy and George Stranger.

Jacob Murrell was the Falkirk man on the scoresheet, having headed into the roof of the net partway through the first half.

It's somewhat rare to see a "smash and grab" home performance, but that is exactly what St. Mirren did this weekend as they picked up a 2-1 win over Dundee despite being under fire for large parts of the game.

Wing-back Calvin Ramsay gave the Paisley side an early lead when he tucked the ball home after 20 minutes, before Eseosa Sule doubled his side's advantage shortly after half-time.

Bradley Fink provided Dundee with a lifeline in the 74th minute, but it was too little, too late for Steven Pressley's side, who passed up too many chances at The Marbill Coaches Stadium.

Sunday's action kicked off in the capital, where Celtic continued their strong start to the season with a comfortable win over Hibernian at Easter Road.

Hibs opened the scoring in the first few minutes of the match, when a quick free-kick found Owen Elding, who made no mistake with the finish. Their lead didn't last long though, with Jason Kerr heading into his own net just two minutes later, bringing Celtic back level.

Camilo Durán netted the winner for Martin O'Neill's side when he cut inside from the right wing before picking out the far corner with a curling strike.

The final game of the weekend saw Hearts pick up a 2-0 win at Fir Park.

The first goal came through Cláudio Braga on the half-hour mark, when the Portuguese forward headed home from close range.

Motherwell registered 11 shots in the second half, but couldn't make them count and were finished off by a wonderful finish from Calvin Millar late in the day, who picked out the bottom corner from 25 yards.

articles.title: Texas opens as heavy favorite against Mississippi State
articles.summary: The Longhorns are three-score favorite as they welcome the Bulldogs to Austin.
articles.body:
The Texas Longhorns narrowly avoided another late-game disappointment at the hands of the Ole Miss Rebels and opened as a 20.5-point favorite against the Mississippi State Bulldogs, according to FanDuel .

Early in the season, the Bulldogs were one of the country's top offenses, rattling off four straight wins, including a big win over then-ranked Missouri Tigers. However, multiple injuries to star quarterback Kamario Taylor have sapped all of their momentum, dropping three consecutive games, including a pair of blowout losses to Alabama and LSU. Taylor started the game against OU, but left the game early due to another injury, which probably contributed to the Bulldogs' status as heavy underdogs.

Freshman Billy Puckett stepped in for him, throwing just one touchdown pass and two interceptions in his four appearances. They have leaned on running back Fluff Bothwell, who averaged more than 6.5 yards per carry against a salty Oklahoma Sooners defense as OU tries to move up the standings in the season's waning weeks. The Texas front will have it work cut out for them yet again as they try to do their part to dig out of the SEC cellar.

On the other sideline, Texas got a narrow win over the Ole Miss Rebels, but will seemingly be without both star left tackle Trevor Goosby and wide receiver Cam Coleman, who both left the game early due to injury. While there are no official updates on their status for the game against the Bulldogs, Goosby was on crutches Saturday night and Coleman returned to the sideline in street clothes after his early exit.

For the year, Texas is 2-5 against the spread, with the lone covers coming in the opener against Texas State and the narrow victory over the Rebels in Austin. Much like their on-the-field result, Mississippi State started the season 4-0 against the spread, but lost the last three games, dropping the last three against Alabama, LSU, and Oklahoma.

articles.title: South Carolina fans storm field after Tennessee upset. Then things get ugly
articles.summary: South Carolina's field storm after upsetting Tennessee turned chaotic, with videos showing heated confrontations between Vols players and fans.
articles.body:
Shortly after Malik Orsan's 48-yard field goal split the uprights as time expired, handing South Carolina a dramatic 27-24 win over No. 11 Tennessee , garnet-and-black-clad Gamecocks fans poured onto the field to celebrate the victory.

From that jubilation, though, came some altercations that were captured on video and quickly spread on social media.

In the most high-profile example of chippiness, Tennessee linebacker Jeremiah Telander appeared to throw a punch at a South Carolina player before quickly being pulled away by a security guard and Volunteers staffer before things escalated.

Telander wasn't the only Tennessee player to let his emotions get the better of him, either.

In another video that circulated on social media, Vols lineman Daevin Hobbs appeared to shove a Gamecocks fan who looked to be carrying a whiteboard used to diagram plays away from the Tennessee sideline. After pushing the fan, Hobbs grabbed the easel.

Other gear and video equipment from the Vols' sideline was damaged during the field-storming.

Other videos showed South Carolina fans on the field taunting Tennessee players after the game. In one, a Gamecocks fan shouted profanities and waved his hand in the face of Vols defensive lineman Kedric Golston, who turned his head and walked away.

A request for comment to Tennessee from the Knoxville News Sentinel, a part of the USA TODAY Network, was not immediately returned.

Since South Carolina fans immediately stormed the field and didn't give the opposing team an opportunity to clear the field, the Gamecocks stand to be fined $500,000 by the SEC. That money would go directly to Tennessee, which was fined for its field rush against Alabama last week.

The loss dropped the Vols to 6-2 on the season and came one week after a 26-10 victory over the Crimson Tide, which was the No. 7 team in the country at the time. South Carolina and embattled head coach Shane Beamer, meanwhile, improved to 4-3 and secured their second-consecutive win against a top-15 opponent, having beaten then-No. 15 Florida on Oct. 10.

The pressure was on P.J. Fleck and the Gophers to change the narrative against Iowa , and they delivered with a 13-10 win. The offense was clunky all night, but the defense put together an all-time great performance.

Gophers' offensive snap counts vs. Iowa (out of 65)

The Gophers' offensive line was thrown another challenge when Shipp left the game with an injury, which prompted Williams to get the first significant snaps of his career at left guard. Ford played a career-high 23 snaps, which resulted in eight carries for 33 yards.

Top 5 PFF grades on offense (min. 10 snaps)

With no Riley Sunram, Randle, Crowder and Chapman saw expanded roles along the interior of Minnesota's defensive line. Gerlach continues to be a key part of their defensive plan with a career-high 64 defensive snaps.

Top 5 PFF grades on defense (min. 10 snaps)

Gerlach had nine total tackles, and Baranowski had seven, making them two of the highest-graded players on Minnesota's defense. Nestor had one of the worst games of his career last season against Iowa, but he responded with an elite performance this year against his favorite team.

articles.title: 1 trade Commanders must make during 2026 NFL season bye week
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders cannot afford to waste their Week 7 bye waiting for their offense to magically fix itself. Terry McLaurin’s season-ending knee inju...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders cannot afford to waste their Week 7 bye waiting for their offense to magically fix itself. Terry McLaurin 's season-ending knee injury has robbed Jayden Daniels of his most established perimeter weapon. At 1-4-1, Washington needs to find a way to keep its young quarterback developing while salvaging a season that is rapidly slipping away. As such, GM Adam Peters should explore a trade for Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. The deal would carry risks, but the Commanders need to think aggressively before the trade deadline passes.

Washington's 2026 campaign has been defined by missed opportunities and mounting injuries. The Commanders opened with consecutive losses to Philadelphia and Dallas before edging Seattle. A 30-13 defeat to Indianapolis followed, then Washington settled for a 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants. Monday night's 23-17 loss to San Francisco left the team at 1-4-1 entering its bye . Daniels threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns against the 49ers. He showed that the passing game can still produce. However, losing McLaurin leaves Washington without its leading veteran receiver for the remainder of the season.

McLaurin's absence creates a serious problem for an offense that needs to maximize Daniels' arm talent and mobility. Washington still has receiving options, including Stefon Diggs and tight end Chig Okonkwo. However, the team must redistribute targets while finding a dependable threat capable of stretching defenses vertically.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Without a consistent outside weapon, opposing secondaries can crowd the intermediate passing lanes and challenge Washington's receivers underneath. That puts more pressure on Daniels to extend plays and manufacture explosive gains.

Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, and Dyami Brown could help absorb the workload. Still, Washington should not assume that internal adjustments alone will replace McLaurin's impact. The Commanders need a receiver who can win outside, track deep passes, and force defensive coordinators to respect the entire field.

Brian Thomas Jr. is an intriguing target because his skill set complements Daniels' strengths. The two played together at LSU. Their connection helped produce some of the most explosive moments of the Tigers' 2023 offense. Thomas finished that season with 68 catches for 1,177 yards and 17 touchdowns. He had the ability to turn downfield opportunities into game-changing plays.

His NFL production has been uneven recently. After recording 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns in 2024, Thomas managed 707 yards and two touchdowns in 2025. Through six games in 2026, he has just nine receptions for 105 yards and one touchdown.

Those numbers make him a potential buy-low candidate. Thomas still offers the long-striding acceleration, catch-point ability, and downfield tracking. Those could transform the Commanders' passing attack.

Pairing him with Diggs would give Daniels a more balanced receiving group. Diggs could work the intermediate areas, while Thomas stretches coverage. That would create opportunities for Okonkwo underneath. Their complementary roles would give offensive coordinator David Blough greater flexibility with formations and route combinations.

Washington should begin negotiations with a 2027 third-round pick and a conditional 2028 fifth-round selection. That package would give Jacksonville meaningful future draft capital without forcing the Commanders to surrender a first-round pick.

Thomas remains a young player with substantial upside. The Jaguars have little incentive to move him cheaply while pursuing their own goals. Washington would need to offer sufficient compensation and ensure that the financial implications fit its long-term plans.

The Commanders must also consider whether one receiver can meaningfully change this campaign's trajectory. Thomas would not fix the offensive line or resolve every issue on defense. However, he could provide the offense with a reliable vertical threat for the rest of the season.

Washington's bye week presents a valuable window to evaluate its needs and explore realistic upgrades. Standing pat would force the remaining receiving corps to take on expanded roles with little margin for error.

Thomas is not a guaranteed solution, of course. Also, Jacksonville may refuse to entertain offers. Still, the potential fit is compelling enough to justify a serious call. The Commanders need to protect Jayden Daniels ' development, restore balance to their passing game, and give their offense a chance to compete.

Peters should pursue Thomas at a sensible price. With this, Washington can take a meaningful step toward rebuilding its offensive identity. A reunion between Daniels and Thomas would offer a promising place to start.

articles.title: Fernandes left out - Man Utd hammered, Bournemouth brilliant - how they rated
articles.summary: Another catastrophic day for Manchester United and a glorious one for Bournemouth - how did the players rate?
articles.body:
Another desperate day for Manchester United as Bournemouth win at Old Trafford for the third time in four years.

United captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped to the bench by manager Michael Carrick and stayed there as the Cherries comfortably won 3-0.

Senne Lammens: Another of those games where everything is looking solid - until it isn't. Massive error for Bournemouth's third goal. 4

Leny Yoro: Vital clearance to deny Evanilson a tap-in. Had situation under control but then slipped to gift Bournemouth their second. 5

Harry Maguire: Regained the captain's armband taken off him by Erik ten Hag. Blocked early Rayan chance and surged forward to try and create at the other end. 6

Ayden Heaven (off 64, Martinez): Some good moments and lots of promise but plenty being asked of the 20-year-old. Yellow card for jumping into a tackle Evanilson jumped out of the way of. Proved to be costly with the resulting free-kick leading to Bournemouth's opener. 5

Diogo Dalot: Got forward well but shooting erratic and pass straight to Evanilson inside own half didn't inspire confidence. Tried to rouse his team but didn't have a lot of success. 5

Carlos Baleba (off, 72, Zirkzee): Not scared to take a risk despite the pressure his team are playing under. Does give United drive in central areas. 5

Andrey Santos: Tielemans' poor control forced him into a rash tackle on Truffert that brought a yellow card. Not much of an impact. 4

Amad Diallo (off 78, Amad): Beautiful bit of skill took him past Truffert but seen too infrequently and passing not accurate enough. 4

Youri Tielemans (off 46, Cunha): Not secure enough in possession for the job Carrick wanted from him. Big disappointment. Off at half-time. 4

Mason Mount: Alternated positions with Tielemans and tried to get on the ball. Thought he was crossing for a team-mate and annoyed when no-one moved for it. 5

Bryan Mbeumo: Hardly in the game until released for shot late in first-half. Had another effort in second half. 6

Matheus Cunha (on 46, Tielemans): Introduced at half-time and did manage a curling effort from edge of the area, which was off target. 6

Lisandro Martinez (on 64, Heaven): Nearly gave away a third goal, and nearly scored one at the other end. 6

Joshua Zirkzee (on 72, Baleba): Not even a consolation goal today. 5

Subs not used: Darlow, Mazraoui, De Ligt, Fernandes, T Fletcher.

Dorde Petrovic: Quiet game until called upon to turn away Mbeumo effort. 6

James Hill: Ambitious long ball to no-one, then crucial interception of Youri Tielemans' low cross before it reached Mbeumo. Solid when pressure mounted. 6

Adam Smith (off 87, Diakite): Man Utd didn't play with conventional wide player, but didn't get drawn out of position. Matched Diogo Dalot when he started running at him after half-time. 6

Antonio Silva: Cruised through the majority of the first half. Busier in the second but always had situation under control. 7

Adrien Truffert: Seized on Yoro error to create the visitors second. 7

Lewis Cook: Quietly effective. Read the game well and stepped in to make challenges and win the ball when required. 7

Tyler Adams: Booked for chopping down Tielemans and wrong side of Mbeumo when he went down but held sway in midfield duel. 7

Rayan: Found space around Dalot in the early stages but didn't make the most of it. Better delivery was nearly converted by Evanilson and superb first-time finish for opener. Should have had a second. 8

Marcus Tavernier (off 87, Adli): Got free on the left on a couple of occasions but couldn't pick out a team-mate with his cross. Easiest of finishes for Bournemouth's second. 8

Justin Kluivert (off, Gannon-Doak, 62): Brilliant free-kick to create the opener. Another eye-catching display. 7

Evanilson (off 87, Kroupi): Close to opener with attempted diving header and did have a goal ruled out for offside. Brilliant finish for the third. 8

Ben Gannon-Doak (on 62, Kluivert): Settled in easily to game that was already set. 7

Ryan Christie (on 75, Cook): Easy game. 6

Subs not used: Di Gregorio, Soler, Brooks, Rodriguez.
